'''Jordan Williams''' (born October 11, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played two seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]].

==High school career==
Williams played high school basketball for [[Torrington High School]] in [[Torrington, Connecticut]].  He averaged 36 points a game as a senior in high school.<ref name=bsun20Feb2010>{{cite news|last=Markus|first=Don|title=Maryland's Williams exceeds expectations|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2010/02/20/marylands-williams-exceeds-expectations/|access-date=January 22, 2011|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=February 20, 2010}}</ref>   Due to questions about the level of his competition, Williams did not receive heavy publicity or recruiting attention in high school.<ref name=bsun20Feb2010 /><ref name=washpost18Nov2010>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Liz|title=Jordan Williams, Maryland basketball ready for first true challenge of the season|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/11/17/AR2010111706352.html?sid=ST2010111706692|access-date=January 22, 2011|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=November 18, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams committed to [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] on October 21, 2008.

===Freshman===
Williams started 31 games as a freshman for the [[2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team]].  He was an All-ACC rookie team selection.  Williams finished second in rebounding in [[2009–10 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|the ACC]].<ref name=umterps>{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Jordan Williams |url=http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/williams_jordan00.html |work=UMTerps.com |access-date=January 22, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110514204526/http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/williams_jordan00.html |archive-date=May 14, 2011 }}</ref>   Maryland coach [[Gary Williams]] complimented Williams' growth as a player as the season progressed.<ref name=bsun20Feb2010 />

===Sophomore===
Before his sophomore season, Williams was named  to the preseason watch list for the [[Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]] watchlists.<ref name=washpost18Nov2010 />   In a January 22, 2011 victory over [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], Williams recorded his thirteenth straight [[Double-double]], which set a Maryland record.  He broke a streak previously held by [[Len Elmore]].<ref name=wpost22Jan2011>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Liz|title=Maryland vs. Clemson: Late free throws help Terrapins hold off Tigers|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2011/01/22/AR2011012202981.html|access-date=January 22, 2011|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=January 22, 2011}}</ref> He was picked to the Third Team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010–11 All-America teams |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }}</ref>

After the season, Williams submitted his name to the NBA draft.  Initially, he did not sign with an agent, which left open the possibility of staying in college.<ref name=wpost29Mar2011>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Liz|title=Maryland's Jordan Williams submits for NBA draft|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/marylands-jordan-williams-submits-for-nba-draft/2011/03/29/AFskhgyB_story.html|access-date=March 30, 2011|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|date=March 29, 2011}}</ref>  He later hired an agent, which precluded a return to collegiate basketball.<ref name=csnwash>{{cite web|last=Standig|first=Benjamin|title=Jordan Williams going pro|url=http://www.csnwashington.com/05/04/11/Jordan-Williams-going-pro/landing.html?blockID=516616&feedID=276|work=[[Comcast Sports Net|CSN Washington]]|access-date=May 6, 2011}}{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 23, 2011, the New Jersey Nets drafted Williams with the 36th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref name=RA_draft>{{cite web|last=Daigneault|first=Ed|title=Nets have spot ready for Jordan to fill Torrington star ready for next step|url=http://www.rep-am.com/articles/2011/06/28/sports/pro/567389.txt|work=[[Republican-American]]|access-date=June 28, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110701184851/http://www.rep-am.com/articles/2011/06/28/sports/pro/567389.txt|archive-date=July 1, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], he agreed to play for the [[Poland|Polish]] team [[Zastal Zielona Góra]]. However, the lockout ended before he played a game for them.<ref>[http://www.netsdaily.com/2011/11/27/2589923/bogdanovic-scores-9-in-tbl-win Bogdanovic Scores 9 in TBL Win; Jordan Williams Heads Back to U.S.]</ref>

Williams was assigned to the [[Springfield Armor]] in January 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/JWill_Armor_Release_120118.html Nets Assign Jordan Williams to Springfield Armor]</ref> Later that month, Williams was recalled by the Nets.

On July 11, 2012, the Nets traded Williams, [[Johan Petro]], [[Jordan Farmar]], [[Anthony Morrow]], and [[Deshawn Stevenson]] to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]].<ref name="hawkstrade">{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2012_Offseason_Tracker.html#wallace | title=A Jolt of Joe for the Nets | publisher=Brooklyn Nets | date=July 11, 2012 | access-date=July 11, 2012 | author=Couch, Ben}}</ref> The Hawks requested waivers on Williams on September 17, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-jordan-williams ATLANTA HAWKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON JORDAN WILLIAMS]</ref>

On August 28, 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[Bilbao Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BILBAO BASKET announces Jordan Williams|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/116521|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=August 28, 2013|access-date=August 28, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130831112504/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/116521|archive-date=August 31, 2013}}</ref> However, on September 8, he parted ways with the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bilbao, Jordan Williams part ways|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/62980/bilbao-jordan-williams-part-ways.html|date=September 8, 2013|access-date=September 8, 2013|work=Sportando.net}}</ref>
